title: Caching as an Architectural Decision, Not a Speed Hack
objective: Compare cache placements against stated latency and consistency budgets, then record a decision that names its invalidation rule as a number or an explicit event.
whyThisMatters: A cache without a stated stale-read bound is a consistency decision you have not admitted to. Architects who add a cache to 'make it faster' and leave invalidation implicit are choosing eventual consistency by accident — and discovering it in an incident.
evidence: A comparison of at least two cache placements plus a no-cache option, each scored against the same latency budget and consistency budget from a prior task
An ADR stating the chosen placement and the invalidation or TTL rule as a number or an explicit invalidating event
A note walking through one stale-read scenario that names the maximum age of the stale value under the chosen rule
acceptanceCriteria: At least two cache placements and a no-cache option are scored against the same stated latency and consistency budgets, not against a general preference.
The ADR states the invalidation rule as a TTL in seconds or as a named event that drops or refreshes the entry.
The stale-read note names a concrete read, the value that would be wrong, and the maximum age of that wrong value under the chosen rule.
